original_question: For a finite group G, the power graph P(G) is the graph with vertex set G and edges {x, y} for all x ̸= y ∈ G such that either x ∈ ⟨y⟩ or y ∈ ⟨x⟩. Is it true that, for every finite group G, if P(G) is a cograph, then P(G) is chordal? Cf. 21.23. This holds if every element of G has prime power order(D. Bubboloni, F. Fumagalli, C. E. Praeger, Preprint, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18073) and if G is a nonabelian simple group(J. Cameron, P. Manna, R. Mehatari, J. Algebra, 591(2022), 59–74; J. Brachter, E. Kaja, J. Algebr. Comb., 58(2023), 1095–1124).

refined_question: Let G be a finite group, and let P(G) be the power graph with vertex set G, where distinct vertices x,y in G are adjacent if and only if x belongs to <y> or y belongs to <x>. A cograph is a graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to a path on 4 vertices, and a chordal graph is a graph with no induced cycle C_n for any n >= 4. Must it be true that, for every finite group G, if P(G) is a cograph, then P(G) is chordal? ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 21.24, so the right refinement is not to broaden it to a classification problem or to enhanced power graphs, but simply to make the notebook's cross-referenced definitions explicit. Problem 21.24 gives the universal finite-group question, while Problem 21.23 supplies the definitions of cograph and chordal that 21.24 invokes by "Cf. 21.23". I therefore kept exactly the same scope and adjacency relation, and only resolved the hidden dependence on the preceding problem so that the question stands on its own. ([alglog.org](https://alglog.org/21tkt.pdf?utm_source=openai))
